title: Text Neck Syndrome
content:
Neck strain from prolonged phone or laptop use.

Indicators:
- Pain after screen use
- Forward head posture
- Upper back tightness

Treatment:
Posture correction and mobility work.

Exercises:
Chin tucks, thoracic extension.

Recovery:
3–8 weeks.

title: Whiplash Injury
content:
Acceleration-deceleration neck trauma.

Indicators:
- Neck stiffness
- Headache
- Limited motion after accident

Treatment:
Gradual mobility, physical therapy.

Exercises:
ROM drills, light isometrics.

Recovery:
2–8 weeks.

title: Neck Muscle Strain
content:
Overstretch or overload of neck muscles.

Indicators:
- Local soreness
- Pain with movement
- No arm radiation

Treatment:
Rest, heat, manual therapy.

Exercises:
Gentle stretching and strengthening.

Recovery:
1–4 weeks.

title: Cervical Radiculopathy
content:
Compression of cervical nerve root.

Indicators:
- Arm numbness
- Radiating pain
- Tingling in hand

Treatment:
Physical therapy, posture correction.

Exercises:
Nerve glides, chin tucks.

Recovery:
3–10 weeks.

title: Cervical Disc Herniation
content:
Disc bulge pressing on cervical nerves.

Indicators:
- Severe neck pain
- Arm weakness
- Symptoms worse with coughing

Treatment:
Medical evaluation, PT.

Exercises:
Extension drills, deep neck flexor work.

Recovery:
6–12 weeks.

title: Cervical Spondylosis
content:
Degenerative arthritis of cervical spine.

Indicators:
- Chronic stiffness
- Reduced mobility
- Age-related pain

Treatment:
Mobility and strengthening program.

Exercises:
Neck stabilization drills.

Recovery:
Chronic condition, symptom-managed.

title: Shoulder Impingement Syndrome
content:
Compression of rotator cuff under acromion.

Indicators:
- Pain lifting arm overhead
- Weakness
- Night discomfort

Treatment:
Load management, PT.

Exercises:
Rotator cuff strengthening, scapular control.

Recovery:
4–10 weeks.

title: Rotator Cuff Tear
content:
Partial or full tear of shoulder tendons.

Indicators:
- Weak lifting
- Pain with rotation
- Limited overhead motion

Treatment:
PT or surgery (severe cases).

Exercises:
Strengthening after inflammation reduces.

Recovery:
8–16 weeks (non-surgical).

title: ACL Tear
content:
Anterior cruciate ligament injury in knee.

Indicators:
- Popping sound
- Knee instability
- Swelling after pivoting

Treatment:
Surgery for athletes, rehab required.

Exercises:
Quadriceps strengthening, balance training.

Recovery:
6–9 months post-surgery.

title: PCL Tear
content:
Posterior cruciate ligament injury.

Indicators:
- Knee pain after fall on bent knee
- Instability descending stairs
- Mild swelling

Treatment:
Bracing and rehabilitation.

Exercises:
Hamstring control, quad strengthening.

Recovery:
3–6 months.

title: Meniscus Tear
content:
Tear in knee cartilage from twisting or degeneration.

Indicators:
- Knee locking or catching
- Swelling after activity
- Pain with deep squatting

Treatment:
Physical therapy, possible surgery.

Exercises:
Quad sets, straight leg raises.

Recovery:
4–8 weeks (conservative), 3–6 months (post-surgery).

title: Patellofemoral Pain Syndrome
content:
Anterior knee pain from kneecap tracking issues.

Indicators:
- Pain around kneecap
- Worse with stairs or sitting
- Crepitus during movement

Treatment:
Strengthening and activity modification.

Exercises:
VMO strengthening, hip abductor work.

Recovery:
6–12 weeks.

title: Patellar Tendinitis
content:
Inflammation of patellar tendon (jumper's knee).

Indicators:
- Pain below kneecap
- Worse with jumping or running
- Tender to touch

Treatment:
Load management, eccentric exercises.

Exercises:
Eccentric squats, decline squats.

Recovery:
6–12 weeks.

title: IT Band Syndrome
content:
Friction of iliotibial band over lateral knee.

Indicators:
- Lateral knee pain
- Worse with running downhill
- Pain at 30° knee flexion

Treatment:
Stretching, foam rolling, strengthening.

Exercises:
Hip abductor strengthening, IT band stretches.

Recovery:
4–8 weeks.

title: Ankle Sprain
content:
Ligament injury from inversion or eversion.

Indicators:
- Swelling and bruising
- Pain bearing weight
- Instability

Treatment:
RICE, progressive loading.

Exercises:
Balance training, calf raises.

Recovery:
2–6 weeks (grade I-II), 8–12 weeks (grade III).

title: Achilles Tendinitis
content:
Overuse inflammation of Achilles tendon.

Indicators:
- Heel pain above ankle
- Morning stiffness
- Pain with running or jumping

Treatment:
Eccentric loading, activity modification.

Exercises:
Heel drops, calf stretches.

Recovery:
6–12 weeks.

title: Plantar Fasciitis
content:
Inflammation of plantar fascia causing heel pain.

Indicators:
- Sharp heel pain with first steps
- Worse in morning
- Pain with prolonged standing

Treatment:
Stretching, orthotics, night splints.

Exercises:
Calf stretches, toe curls, foot rolling.

Recovery:
6–18 months.

title: Frozen Shoulder
content:
Adhesive capsulitis causing severe shoulder stiffness.

Indicators:
- Progressive loss of motion
- Night pain
- Difficulty with ADLs

Treatment:
Mobilization, gentle stretching, sometimes cortisone.

Exercises:
Pendulum exercises, wall walks.

Recovery:
12–36 months.

title: Tennis Elbow
content:
Lateral epicondylitis from overuse of forearm extensors.

Indicators:
- Lateral elbow pain
- Weak grip strength
- Pain with wrist extension

Treatment:
Rest, eccentric exercises, bracing.

Exercises:
Wrist extension exercises, forearm stretches.

Recovery:
6–12 weeks.

title: Golfer's Elbow
content:
Medial epicondylitis affecting wrist flexors.

Indicators:
- Medial elbow pain
- Pain with gripping
- Tenderness on inner elbow

Treatment:
Activity modification, strengthening.

Exercises:
Wrist flexor stretches, eccentric loading.

Recovery:
6–12 weeks.

title: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome
content:
Median nerve compression at wrist.

Indicators:
- Numbness in thumb, index, middle fingers
- Night symptoms
- Weakness in grip

Treatment:
Splinting, nerve glides, possible surgery.

Exercises:
Median nerve glides, wrist stretches.

Recovery:
6–12 weeks (conservative), 3–6 months (post-surgery).

title: Lower Back Strain
content:
Muscle or ligament strain in lumbar region.

Indicators:
- Localized lower back pain
- Muscle spasm
- Pain with bending or lifting

Treatment:
Rest, heat, gradual return to activity.

Exercises:
Core stabilization, gentle stretching.

Recovery:
2–6 weeks.

title: Lumbar Disc Herniation
content:
Disc bulge or rupture in lower back.

Indicators:
- Radiating leg pain (sciatica)
- Numbness or tingling
- Worse with sitting or coughing

Treatment:
Physical therapy, epidural injections, surgery if severe.

Exercises:
McKenzie extensions, core work.

Recovery:
6–12 weeks (conservative), 3–6 months (post-surgery).

title: Sciatica
content:
Sciatic nerve irritation causing leg pain.

Indicators:
- Pain radiating from back to leg
- Burning or shooting pain
- Numbness in leg or foot

Treatment:
Nerve mobilization, posture correction.

Exercises:
Nerve flossing, piriformis stretches.

Recovery:
4–12 weeks.

title: Piriformis Syndrome
content:
Piriformis muscle compressing sciatic nerve.

Indicators:
- Deep buttock pain
- Pain with sitting
- Radiating leg symptoms

Treatment:
Stretching, manual therapy.

Exercises:
Piriformis stretches, hip strengthening.

Recovery:
4–8 weeks.

title: Hip Bursitis
content:
Inflammation of bursa on lateral hip.

Indicators:
- Lateral hip pain
- Pain lying on affected side
- Tenderness over greater trochanter

Treatment:
Activity modification, anti-inflammatories.

Exercises:
Hip abductor strengthening, ITB stretches.

Recovery:
4–8 weeks.

title: Hip Labral Tear
content:
Tear in cartilage ring around hip socket.

Indicators:
- Deep groin pain
- Clicking or locking
- Pain with hip flexion and rotation

Treatment:
Physical therapy, possible surgery.

Exercises:
Hip stabilization, controlled mobility.

Recovery:
8–12 weeks (conservative), 4–6 months (post-surgery).

title: Hamstring Strain
content:
Tear or overstretching of hamstring muscles.

Indicators:
- Sudden posterior thigh pain
- Bruising possible
- Pain with knee flexion

Treatment:
RICE, progressive loading.

Exercises:
Eccentric hamstring curls, Nordic curls.

Recovery:
2–3 weeks (grade I), 4–8 weeks (grade II), 3+ months (grade III).

title: Groin Strain
content:
Adductor muscle injury in inner thigh.

Indicators:
- Inner thigh pain
- Pain with kicking or direction changes
- Tenderness along adductors

Treatment:
Rest, progressive strengthening.

Exercises:
Adductor squeezes, side lunges.

Recovery:
2–6 weeks.

title: Quadriceps Strain
content:
Tear or overstretch of quadriceps muscles.

Indicators:
- Anterior thigh pain
- Weakness extending knee
- Visible bruising possible

Treatment:
RICE, gradual return to activity.

Exercises:
Isometric quads, progressive resistance.

Recovery:
2–8 weeks depending on severity.

title: Shin Splints
content:
Medial tibial stress syndrome from overuse.

Indicators:
- Pain along inner shin
- Worse with running
- Tender to touch

Treatment:
Rest, ice, gradual return to running.

Exercises:
Calf strengthening, ankle mobility.

Recovery:
3–6 weeks.

title: Calf Strain
content:
Tear in gastrocnemius or soleus muscles.

Indicators:
- Sudden calf pain
- Difficulty walking on toes
- Possible bruising

Treatment:
RICE, progressive loading.

Exercises:
Calf raises, eccentric heel drops.

Recovery:
2–6 weeks.

title: Stress Fracture
content:
Overuse bone injury from repetitive loading.

Indicators:
- Localized bone pain
- Worse with activity, better with rest
- Point tenderness

Treatment:
Rest, possible boot/crutches.

Exercises:
Maintain fitness with non-impact activities.

Recovery:
6–12 weeks.

title: Biceps Tendinitis
content:
Inflammation of long head of biceps tendon.

Indicators:
- Anterior shoulder pain
- Pain with overhead activities
- Tender biceps groove

Treatment:
Rest, anti-inflammatories, PT.

Exercises:
Biceps stretches, rotator cuff work.

Recovery:
4–8 weeks.

title: Shoulder Dislocation
content:
Humeral head displaced from glenoid socket.

Indicators:
- Severe pain
- Visible deformity
- Loss of motion

Treatment:
Reduction, immobilization, then rehab.

Exercises:
Gradual ROM, then strengthening.

Recovery:
3–6 months.

title: AC Joint Separation
content:
Acromioclavicular ligament injury.

Indicators:
- Pain over top of shoulder
- Visible bump if severe
- Pain with cross-body movements

Treatment:
Sling, PT, surgery for grade III+.

Exercises:
Scapular stabilization, deltoid work.

Recovery:
2–6 weeks (grade I-II), 3–6 months (grade III+).

title: Thoracic Outlet Syndrome
content:
Compression of nerves/vessels between neck and shoulder.

Indicators:
- Numbness in arm/hand
- Weakness
- Symptoms worse with arm overhead

Treatment:
Posture correction, stretching, strengthening.

Exercises:
Scalene stretches, pec stretches.

Recovery:
6–12 weeks.

title: Scoliosis
content:
Lateral curvature of spine.

Indicators:
- Visible spinal curve
- Uneven shoulders/hips
- Back pain in some cases

Treatment:
Physical therapy, bracing if severe, surgery in extreme cases.

Exercises:
Core strengthening, asymmetric stretches.

Recovery:
Chronic condition, managed long-term.

title: Lumbar Spinal Stenosis
content:
Narrowing of spinal canal in lower back.

Indicators:
- Leg pain with walking
- Relief when sitting or bending forward
- Bilateral symptoms possible

Treatment:
Physical therapy, epidurals, surgery if severe.

Exercises:
Flexion-based exercises, core work.

Recovery:
Chronic condition, symptom management.

title: Sacroiliac Joint Dysfunction
content:
Pain from SI joint inflammation or hypomobility.

Indicators:
- Lower back pain (usually one-sided)
- Pain in buttock or groin
- Worse with stairs or standing from sitting

Treatment:
Manual therapy, stabilization exercises.

Exercises:
Core and hip strengthening, SI joint mobilization.

Recovery:
4–8 weeks.

title: De Quervain's Tenosynovitis
content:
Inflammation of thumb tendons at wrist.

Indicators:
- Pain at thumb side of wrist
- Swelling
- Positive Finkelstein test

Treatment:
Splinting, anti-inflammatories, sometimes injection.

Exercises:
Gentle thumb stretches after inflammation subsides.

Recovery:
4–8 weeks.

title: Trigger Finger
content:
Locking or catching of finger due to tendon inflammation.

Indicators:
- Finger catching or locking
- Morning stiffness
- Painful nodule at base of finger

Treatment:
Splinting, injections, surgery if persistent.

Exercises:
Gentle finger stretches.

Recovery:
4–8 weeks (conservative), 2–4 weeks (post-surgery).

title: Morton's Neuroma
content:
Nerve thickening between toes causing pain.

Indicators:
- Burning pain in ball of foot
- Numbness in toes
- Feels like standing on marble

Treatment:
Wider shoes, orthotics, injections, surgery.

Exercises:
Toe stretches, foot mobilization.

Recovery:
6–12 weeks (conservative).

title: Turf Toe
content:
Hyperextension injury to big toe joint.

Indicators:
- Pain at base of big toe
- Swelling
- Difficulty pushing off

Treatment:
RICE, taping, stiff-soled shoes.

Exercises:
Gentle ROM after acute phase.

Recovery:
2–6 weeks.

title: Peroneal Tendinitis
content:
Inflammation of peroneal tendons on outside of ankle.

Indicators:
- Lateral ankle pain
- Pain with eversion
- Worse with activity

Treatment:
Rest, ice, strengthening.

Exercises:
Peroneal strengthening, balance training.

Recovery:
4–8 weeks.

title: Osgood-Schlatter Disease
content:
Growth plate inflammation at tibial tuberosity in adolescents.

Indicators:
- Bump below kneecap
- Pain with running/jumping
- Tender to touch

Treatment:
Activity modification, ice, stretching.

Exercises:
Quad and hamstring stretches.

Recovery:
Resolves with skeletal maturity, symptoms managed 6–24 months.

title: Sever's Disease
content:
Growth plate inflammation at heel in children.

Indicators:
- Heel pain in growing child
- Worse with activity
- Limping

Treatment:
Rest, heel lifts, ice.

Exercises:
Calf stretches.

Recovery:
Resolves with skeletal maturity, 6–12 months.

title: Bursitis (General)
content:
Inflammation of fluid-filled sac cushioning joints.

Indicators:
- Localized swelling
- Pain with movement
- Warmth and redness possible

Treatment:
Rest, ice, anti-inflammatories, aspiration if large.

Exercises:
Gentle ROM after acute inflammation subsides.

Recovery:
2–6 weeks.
